name: record_interpretation
arguments: {"test_id": "T1", "per_hypothesis": [{"id": "H1", "verdict": "unchanged", "why": "T1 measures folding free energy, not phosphotyrosine binding, so it does not test the SH2 pocket model. The would_refute criterion (docked pY more than about 4.5 \u00c5 from Arg288, or equal W288 docking energy) was not evaluated. Context only: the same predictor gives R288Q a \u0394\u0394G of +0.13 kcal/mol, so the destabilisation is driven by the Trp side chain, not by loss of charge. That does not bear on H1's binding mechanism either way."}, {"id": "H2", "verdict": "supported", "why": "FoldX \u0394\u0394G for R288W is +5.68 kcal/mol on AF-Q06187-F1, above the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold (verdict predicted_destabilising). Applicability passed: residue pLDDT 85.06. Within-site comparison: R288G +0.49 and R288Q +0.13 kcal/mol, so this substitution stands out at the site. The would_refute criterion (|\u0394\u0394G| within about 1 kcal/mol) was not met, so H2 is not refuted. Consistent with E4 (helix 288-298), E13 (pLDDT 84.44) and E6-E9 (computational pathogenicity signals)."}], "uncertainty": "T1 is one computational FoldX estimate on one predicted model. FoldX errors on predicted models are near 1 kcal/mol, so +5.68 is well outside that band, but it is still not a measurement. The missense3d result (Neutral) conflicts with the FoldX call and is not explained by the record; treat it as a disagreement, not as support for either side. A neutral stability call does not show the variant is tolerated, and this test cannot show whether destabilisation reduces expression, causes misfolding in cells, or is only one part of the loss of function. ClinVar also lists R288Q as pathogenic (E14) while FoldX calls R288Q nearly neutral (+0.13), so a folding-only model does not explain the whole residue, and a binding mechanism (H1) may still contribute. The runner returned no job ID or manifest URL; provenance rests on results/T1.json and the reproducible command in the record, so the run cannot be independently traced to a remote job. Validation still needed: an independent stability predictor (for example ESM-based or a second FoldX run with repair), and a wet-lab expression or thermal-stability measurement of R288W."}

name: record_decision
arguments: {"favoured_after": "H2", "why": "Previous favourite H1 (protein interaction): its direct support is residue-level, not substitution-level. E15 (PMID 11206059) reports that R288 and R307 in the phosphotyrosine pocket cut peptide binding more than 200-fold, and E10/E11 show the residue at the SH2 pocket. No measurement exists for R288W binding, and T3 (ligand contact) is not feasible (feasibility 0). Strongest rival H2 (stability/folding): T1 (predicted_destabilising, \u0394\u0394G +5.68 kcal/mol, residue pLDDT 85.06, within-site R288G +0.49 and R288Q +0.13) gives a measured value for this exact substitution that passed its applicability control, and does not meet H2's refutation criterion. E4, E13 and E6-E9 already supported H2. Given that T1 adds the only direct R288W number and H1 has no direct R288W binding measurement, H2 now has the stronger direct support. This is a computational prediction, not an experiment, and E14 (R288Q pathogenic, FoldX near neutral) means H1 is not excluded. Evidence: T1, E4, E13, E15, E14."}
